title: Switch cleanly through the target instead of stab-clicking every rep
summary: Speed and evasive switching families like DOTTS and DriftTS reward a smooth switch plus stable finish, not just a sharp first snap on every target.
why: Switching score is often lost in the finish and exit, not only in the first snap.
Hold-fire and continuous-acquisition tasks punish stop-start switching patterns that look fast for one instant but break the chain.
actions: Flow into the target and stabilize the finish instead of hard resetting every switch.
Judge the whole kill chain, including exit quality, rather than only how fast the cursor first arrived.
If the snap is fast but the finish is messy, slow the switch slightly until the continuous finish is cleaner.
avoid: Do not reduce hold-fire switching to repeated stab-click behavior.
Avoid trading finish quality away for one flashy initial snap.

drills.label: Voltaic S5 DOTTS / DriftTS
drills.reason: These switching families expose whether the player can keep chaining quality through the finish of each acquisition.

evidence.claim: DOTTS and DriftTS-style switching reward smooth entry, micro-correction, and finish quality rather than only raw first-snap speed.
evidence.excerpt: Voltaic describes DOTTS, DriftTS, and PentabounceTS as switching families with distinct emphasis on finish quality and control.
